newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 24.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Yesterday, the cabinet approved the sale of the state's stake in IPB bank to Japanese Nomura. The state owns 31.48 percent through the National Property Fund and 4.45 percent through Ceska Posta.

- From August 15, the first citizens from areas affected by the floods who lost their homes could receive state grants of 150,000 crowns for housing and possible state loans of up to 850,000 crowns according to a cabinet decision.
- The cabinet did not approve the sale of 100 modernised T-72 tanks to Algeria.
- The travel agency East West Travel proposed to make itself bankrupt yesterday. After Oasis Tours and Travela, it is the third travel agency to go under.
- Ministers decided yesterday that they will take their holidays progressively. There will be no Wednesday cabinet meetings for the next two weeks.
- There should be a tripartite meeting today to decide on changing statutes and the structure of the council.
- The dominant domestic fuel manufacturer, Ceska Rafinerska a.s. had gross profits of 580 million crowns in the first half of this year, a year-on-year increase of 38 percent.
- During trading yesterday, the crown strengthened and ended at 18.77 to the mark and 34.28 to the dollar.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - According to a proposal approved by the cabinet yesterday for a new law on banks, domestic banks will have to separate their commercial and investment activities.
- Shares of Chemopetrol Group and Kaucuk Group will be traded on the Prague Stock Exchange for the last time this Friday. The companies will become part of Unipetrol.

- Minority shareholders proposed to liquidate the Czech National Investment Property Fund and the Czech National Investment Trading Business Fund. A decision will be made during general meetings in August.
- A new company is on the scene of Poldi Steel; Mossei International Holding wants to buy nearly half of the company for 250 million crowns and promises to invest one billion crowns.

- The Anti-monopoly Office approved a merger of the large spice company Emarko Varnsdorf and the largest rice processor in the country, Bask Roudnice, because joining the companies should bring consumers many advantages.
- The cabinet decided yesterday that the speed limit on highways will increase to 130 kilometres per hour from 110. The speed limit in built-up areas will remain at 60 kilometres per hour.
PRAVO - The cabinet approved a proposal for health insurance yesterday. Patients' payments should increase by 100 percent if the proposal is approved by parliament.
- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus called on citizens to have a minute of silence today at noon to comemorate flood victims.
- In a general meeting, shareholders of Kovohute Bridlicina approved an increase in basic capital by 0.5 billion crowns and to issue bonds of one billion crowns between November and December.

- The president of the industry and transport union, Stepan Popovic, said the import deposit should have been cancelled the moment the crown was devalued. He said it is a measure which only brings profits for banks.

LIDOVE NOVINY - From August 1, RM-System is increasing payments from direct transactions. For shares, the rate will be 0.1 percent and for bonds 0.02 percent, but always at least 50 crowns and no more than 500 crowns.
- The cabinet decided to reduce the number of hospital beds in 27 districts by one fifth.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
